stowegardens.heading: The Stowe Ranger
stowegardens.about: I met with Head Ranger Barry Smith to find out more about the challenge of managing the flora and fauna and preparing it for the future.

buckingham_canal_society.heading: Buckingham Canal Society
buckingham_canal_society.about: I met with Athena Beckett to find out more about the work of the Buckingham Canal Society.

river_rinse.heading: Buckingham River Rinse
river_rinse.about: September in Buckingham means it's time to get the river back in shape. What's on in Buckingham

bard_of_stony.heading: Bard of Stony Stratford
bard_of_stony.about: Nova Carmen, Bard of Stony Stratford, shares some tips with us on how to get creative. Bard of Stony Stratford

bradwell_abbey.heading: Bradwell Abbey
bradwell_abbey.about: The new city of Milton Keynes contains some ancient gems including this wonderful pilgrimage site. Museum website

bradwell_windmill.heading: Bradwell Windmill
bradwell_windmill.about: With a booming population in London needing flour, an entrepreneur had an idea to build a canal-side windmill. Website

passivhaus.heading: Passivhaus
passivhaus.about: A wander through Manor Park might take you back in time to the Georgian Era, but it's a place where housing of the future is being designed. Eco Design Consultants

cowper_newton_museum.heading: Cowper & Newton Museum
cowper_newton_museum.about: Find out more about a friendship that inspired Amazing Grace. Museum website

emmaus.heading: Emmaus
emmaus.about: It's a charity, a community and a great place to have a break on the Ouse Valley Way. I speak to Lynn Reeves to Operations Manager to find out more.

harrold_odell_country_park.heading: Harrold Odell Country Park
harrold_odell_country_park.about: It's been called the jewell of North Bedfordshire and the Ouse Valley Way passes right through it. I meet Ed Green who shares with us how he keeps this local gem in good order. Park website

john_bunyan.heading: John Bunyan and the Pilgrim's Progress
john_bunyan.about: Between Pavenham and Bromham Mill, the Ouse Valley Way joins another walking route - The John Bunyan Trail. It's an 86 mile loop that seeks to follow in the footsteps of John Bunyan who used to walk these parts as a tinker and preacher. That was before being put in prison and then using his time doing stir to write The Pilgrim's Progress. I met with John Pestell from the Bunyan Museum to find out more about man and his greatest work. Bunyan Museum

guru_nanak_temple.heading: Guru Nanak Gurdwara Temple
guru_nanak_temple.about: There's an impressive temple visible from the Ouse Valley Way, Let's go and visit it.

panacea.heading: An ordinary house?
panacea.about: Ever fancied visiting the actual Garden of Eden? Come for a pot of tea and learn about a society that spend the 20th Century preparing for the Apocalypse.

paxton_pits.heading: Paxton Pits
paxton_pits.about: I met with Paxton Pits ranger, Robyn Staddon to find out more about the nature reserve.

cromwell_museum.heading: Cromwell Museum
cromwell_museum.about: What better place to learn about one of England's most consequential and controversial figures in history.Museum website

stretham_old_engine.heading: Stretham Old Engine
stretham_old_engine.about: The Fens are Britain's bread-basket thanks to the work of pumping stations keeping the land drained. But it's thanks to the work of dedicated volunteers at the 200 year-old Stretham Old Engline that we can learn what it has taken to keep Britain fed. Museum site

stained_glass_museum.heading: Stained Glass Museum
stained_glass_museum.about: Most of the churches along the Ouse Valley Way contain treasures hiding in plain sight - stained glass. Emily Allen from the Stained Glass Museum is going to help us see what we have been looking through. Museum website

cromwells_house.heading: Cromwell's House
cromwells_house.about: An obvious place to start any visit to Ely is at the tourist information office and it comes with an added bonus - it was also Oliver Cromwell’s family home Website

downham.heading: On the Gingerbread Trail
downham.about:
Discover Downham was created by a dedicated group of volunteers who were determined to save the artifacts and stories that tell the history of their town. I met with Kathleen Wiseman who took me on a wander to find out why it's known as the Gingetbread Town.
Discover Downham Website

higgins.heading: Remembering the R101
higgins.about:
Why did the R101's maiden flight end in tragedy? Lydia McDonald helps us find out.
Website

rspb_ouse_fen.heading: RSBP Ouse Fen
rspb_ouse_fen.about:
A project is underway turning quarried land into a unique reserve, based on reedbeds. let's talk to the wardens to find out more.
Website

watermills.heading: Watermilling
watermills.about: It’s a pleasant stroll across the meadows between Godmanchester and St Ives with Houghton Mill being the perfect place to stop for a nice stop for a cup of tea. And it’s here that I met Keith Grimwade and Bridget Flannagan who have done a deep dive into the history and geography of the area and written a book on watermilling along the Great Ouse in Cambridgeshire.Book details
